author: Jeremy Goldstein
title: Aryna Sabalenka responds to being given new nickname after US Open win - NewsBreak
text:
By Jeremy Goldstein ,
45 minutes ago World No. 1 Aryna Sabalenka continued her quest for a second consecutive US Open victory with a nervy second-round win over Polina Kudermetova 7-6 (4), 6-2 on Tuesday night. She'll face former US Open finalist Leylah Fernandez in the third round .
In the process of her win, the Belarusian continued her unprecedented streak of 17 consecutive tiebreak victories. According to OptaAce, her 19 tiebreak wins in a calendar year are the most during the Open Era in Women's Singles.
This led the on-court ESPN reporter to unveil a new nickname, "Aryna Tiebreakalenka." Sabalenka — who relied on tiebreaks to beat Emma Raducanu over the summer in Cincinnati — was then asked: "Why are you so good in the most crucial moments?” The always-humble 27-year-old pleaded the fifth. “Honestly, I don’t know," she answered.

READ MORE: PGA Tour star shows true colors after phone call with Tommy Fleetwood's wife
"I’m just trying to stay aggressive and fight for every point. I know every point can be a key moment of the set, so I’m just trying to stay strong and play aggressively.”
Sabalenka had to dig deep for the win. She served at 5-5 in the first set but fell down 15-40. The 27-year-old staved off two straight break points, won the game, and took the eventual tiebreak.
The win means Sabalenka will face the Canadian No. 31 Fernandez, the same surprising unseeded player who shocked the Belarusian star in the 2021 US Open semifinal. After that loss, Sabalenka admitted she "destroyed herself."
"That’s why I’m a little bit disappointed about this match because, as I said, I had a lot of opportunities and I didn’t use it," she said in 2021. "Well, this is life. If you’re not using your opportunities, someone else will use it. This is what happened today. I will try to improve it.
"I will keep working and fighting, and I believe that one day it will come. I was just sometimes overhitting, sometimes I didn’t move well. As I said, on the key moment, I was up 4-2 serving, and I think I made double-faults. My first-serve percentage wasn’t really good. I wouldn’t say that she did something. I would say that I destroy myself."
If Sabalenka can advance past Fernandez, her quest for a second straight US Open may include a series of further tricky matchups against the likes of Elise Mertens, Emma Raducanu, Jessica Paolini, Jess Pegula, and/or Mirra Andreeva.

After her win over Kudermetova, she was naturally asked what the key is to making another deep run. “I think I have to focus on myself," the 27-year-old said.
"I know if I’m able to bring my game and fight for every point, I know I’ll have my chances. All I try to do is focus on myself and bring the best fight possible every time I’m out here playing in front of you all.
